headline: Bad Football Day Leads to Life-Saving Rescue in English Valley
meta_description: Frustrated Arsenal fan Alastair Cass storms out of his house after a 3-0 loss, only to hear cries for help and rescue a woman trapped chest-high in mud for fou…
summary_short: A Devon businessman's frustration over his team's loss became a woman's salvation when he heard her desperate calls from a muddy ditch and mounted a rescue effort.
body:
When Alastair Cass stormed out of his house in Devon, England, after watching Arsenal lose 3-0 to Brighton, he had no idea the next hours would transform his anger into an act of heroism. Walking across his property, the 40-year-old business owner heard strange cries coming from the valley behind his home. He drove his quad bike toward the sound and eventually made out the word "help"—only to discover a woman named Sallie stuck in mud up to her chest line, having been trapped there for four hours, shivering and unable to move.

Cass immediately attempted a rescue with rope and wooden planks to distribute his weight across the treacherous mud, but the suction was too powerful and caused Sallie such pain that he knew emergency services were her only hope. He raced home to call for help, triggering one of the largest rescue operations the area had seen: the Chulmleigh fire brigade, specialist teams, police, boat rescue service, four ambulance crews, and multiple helicopters all converged on the remote, unkempt gully. The two-hour operation required Cass to make multiple trips up and down the ditch, guiding rescuers and carrying equipment to Sallie's location until she was finally freed to safety.

In her thank-you card, Sallie wrote: "I have never been so happy to see another human being as I was you that day!" She even managed to find humor in the circumstances, adding, "Thanks to Arsenal for being rubbish at football!" For Cass, who has lived on his 150-acre property for 28 years, the unexpected turn proved that sometimes life's frustrations lead us exactly where we're needed most.
quick_facts: Alastair Cass, 40, left his Devon home angry after Arsenal lost 3-0
Woman Sallie trapped chest-high in mud for four hours in valley ditch
Rescue involved fire brigade, police, boat rescue, four ambulances, helicopters
Two-hour operation freed Sallie after Cass heard her cries and called emergency services
